checks: Read work_summary, s47-s50 outputs and the Q4 entries of report.json. Round-1 fixes were all addressed: the 'hint of opacity' (FWHM ratio 1.085+-0.015) was tested against a null built from 190 beam-spaced r<0.15" apertures (median 1.036, 16-84% 0.98-1.09, 17% >= 1.084). That is about 1 sigma of the real scatter, so the claim is correctly withdrawn. A common-beam convolution and a spatial-weights model were also run. The report no longer treats the dip in R(v) as evidence.

Sanity-checked the continuum T_b: 0.18 K at 257.8 GHz and 0.24" corresponds to about 0.56 mJy/beam, which is plausible and far below the line T_b of 1.5-1.9 K. Continuum absorption of HCO+ at S is therefore excluded, and the conclusion follows from the numbers. The cubes are continuum-subtracted, which was noted.

The T_b discriminator (s48) now gives the consequences of each branch. The N core is not separable (thin: A~1-6, log N 14.25-16.5; thick: log N 17.75, eta~0.07). At S, equal-Tex saturated lines are excluded, which is a real constraint. I agree with the conclusion that opacity vs abundance is undecided with these data.

H13CN injection-recovery (s49) models the CO wing in 3 families with 144 realisations per level and window. The false-limit rate is 0/144 and bias is <=0.013, so the limit alpha<0.075-0.12 is credible. The marginal best-fit alpha of 0.02-0.10 is correctly called marginal and wing-degenerate. The worker corrected the band-edge geometry in my round-1 premise, and the corrected version is right: the edge is on the blue side. The thick-core band (s50) carries the limit through to tau_core, with f3 scanned and L_tot taken from the beam-matched ratio. Thick core neither excluded nor required. I agree.
HCN v2=1f 3-2/4-3 limits (alpha<0.01-0.1) and the v2=1e blend inseparability are reported with the appropriate caveats. HNC is not covered, which is stated.
notes_for_questioner: The core opacity vs abundance question can only be settled with H13CN/H13CO+ 3-2 or 4-3 at <0.5" or HNC, none of which are in these data. Say so as a proposal-level recommendation. Is the S HCN/HCO+ Tex ratio of ~0.5-0.6 (or a thin HCN with A<1) consistent with a lower HCN abundance in the S outflow base? This is worth cross-checking against the Q1 radial trend. A ~3x difference in thin-branch A between N and S is the only chemistry-level statement the data support, and it should be reported with the single-zone RADEX caveat.
